score.details.recovery.label: Body Recovery
score.details.recovery.description:
Physical recovery is a very important aspect to take into consideration when checking your overall condition. Especially after high or medium intensity activities, your body and heart need time to repair. When over exercising, there is up to a 72 hours window of impaired immunity. This basically means virus and bacteria may have an easier time infecting your body.

Kira automatically checks your activity volume in the past 48 hours. Medium and high intensity activities combined should not exceed a total of 240 cardio points.


Even though you might be able to do more, the scientific literature is clear on the subject, it is unhealthy to exceed such amounts without recovery and without tiring your muscles and heart.
score.details.wake_up.label: Wake up score
score.details.wake_up.description:
The wake up score measures your level of sleep inertia when you wake up based on the stage you woke up in and what part of that stage you were in.


While it is a great measure to take into consideration for your energy levels, it mostly affects the beginning of your day even though inertia might affect your attention in the afternoon. This is why it has a lighter weight in the calculation of your energy.
score.details.breathing.label: Breathing rate
score.details.breathing.description:
Breathing rate reported in respirations (breaths) per minute is an indicator of your cardiovascular load and is a good indicator of your wellbeing. You breathe harder and faster when you are ill or in need of energy. 


This metric varies much less than your RHR and HRV and is therefore much more stable. It becomes very useful when it increases a lot compared to your Reference. This metric acts as a threshold that can warn you when something is highly unusual. The difference between your daily value and your Reference shows to what degree you are in good condition or not. Normal values for a resting adult ranges from 12 to18 breaths per minute.
score.details.hrv.label: Heart rate variability
score.details.hrv.description:
HRV measures the specific changes in time between successive heartbeats and is a great measure of your autonomic nervous system. It is used to see how well you recover after certain events. It is also a good measure of stress and anxiety and can unveil many things about your overall wellbeing.


HRV is highly personal and variations are measured against your own Reference. Anything above means that your body and immune system are ready to tackle challenges during an upcoming day whereas the contrary would probably mean that you need to focus on recovering, basically resuming a healthy pace of life and sleep well. The difference between your daily value and your Reference shows to what degree you are in good condition or not.
score.details.resting_heart_rate.label: Resting heart rate
score.details.resting_heart_rate.descrip:
RHR is a great measure for your overall health, readiness and fitness. A low resting heart rate is an indication of a strong heart muscle that can pump out a greater amount of blood with every beat so it does not have to beat as frequently. Generally speaking, the lower it is, the better.


A higher RHR compared to your Reference indicates poor overall wellness conditions, that you shoud avoid too much mental and physical stress and concentrate on recovering. If your daily RHR is lower than your Reference then your body is ready for intense stress. 


Kira also compares your Reference with the References of people of the same physiology to assess where you stand in terms of fitness. The difference between your daily value and your Reference shows to what degree you are in good condition or not.
score.details.temperature.label: Temperature variation
score.details.temperature.description:
This contributor looks at the temperature variations occurring throughout your sleep compared to your baseline. It an essential metric to evaluate how your natural defenses respond to your environement. 

When the variation is higher than +/- 0.8 degrees Celcius, that’s when you need to start paying attention. An advice would be measuring your body temperature with a thermometer. 

Any variance above or under your baseline can give a lot of crucial information. It can fluctuate with activity, your nutrition, your circadian rhythm, can indicate that your body fights against an illness, can reflect external environment changes such as a season change and can even reflect a woman’s menstrual cycle very clearly. 

Typically, the pattern for menStrual cycles is a temperature drop from your periods through your ovulation phase, followed by a rise from the end of your ovulation until the beginning of your next periods.
score.details.sleep_quality.label: Sleep quality
score.details.sleep_quality.description:
The Sleep Quality contributor is based on a longer term view of your sleep quality patterns. Having slept very poorly two nights ago, even by having slept well yesterday night will have a negative impact on your energy today.


Kira looks at the past two days of your sleep quality. The sleep quality score takes a number of contributors into consideration to determine whether it was poor, good or optimal.


The main takeaway is to consider that a score below 80 would mean that your overall sleep quality was poor, which will negatively affect the energy levels. On the contrary, anything over 80 is quite good and is a great indicator of how good you will feel throughout the day both physically and mentally.
score.details.sleep_balance.label: Sleep balance
score.details.sleep_balance.description:
The Sleep Balance contributor is based on a long term view of your sleep duration patterns. 


Kira compares the past two days of your sleep duration to your long-term sleep history as well as to the ideal amount of sleep duration for people of your chronotype and age. It's advised that for staying healthy and alert, adults typically need 7-9 hours of sleep every night.
score.details.activity_volume.label: Activity volume
score.details.activity_volume.descriptio:
Activity Volume measures the amount of active minutes you've gotten over the past 7 days. It is an essential aspect of maintaining and improving your fitness level. 


Kira bases her calculations on two key components. One is making sure you are respecting the medical recommendations (at least 300 minutes of active minutes per week) and the other is making sure that you have an activity load that is suitable to your activity habits.

onboarding.wear.info.top:
The best fingers to wear Circular are the <colored>index</colored>, <colored>middle finger</colored>, <colored>ring finger</colored>, pinky finger and thumb.

Try as much as possible to use the same finger and same ring positioning each time you wear your Circular.
onboarding.wear.info.bottom:
The flat part of the ring should be on the <colored>palmar side</colored> of your finger.

The button should be <colored>facing your thumb</colored>, for ease of use.
